expected: The default year should be the one that actually has data -- either the current calendar year or the most recent year present in the ledger -- not a year picked independent of the ledger's contents. A tax page's first impression on a fresh session should not be an absence claim about a ledger that in fact holds every transaction I have made.
observed: Landing on /tax fresh (right after my first two fills) selects tax year 2025 by default (confirmed via document.querySelector('select').value === '2025'). The page reads: 'No 2025 activity at all. The ledger holds 3 transactions, none of them dated in this tax year -- pick another year above.' The ledger's only three transactions -- my deposit and two buys -- are all dated 2026. Switching the select to 2026 immediately surfaces them: 'Nothing was disposed of in 2026. The ledger holds 3 transactions dated in this tax year -- see Activity -- but no lot was sold.'
repro: Fill at least one order so the ledger has 2026-dated transactions.
Note the year <select>'s value is 2025 (one year behind the ledger's actual activity), and the panel below states no 2025 activity exists.
Manually switch the select to 2026 -- the same three transactions are now found and the message changes to the correct 'nothing disposed of' copy.
suggested_fix: Default the year select to the most recent year that has ledger transactions (falling back to the current calendar year if the ledger is empty), rather than a fixed offset from today's date.
title: Tax page's default year selection has no activity, reads as an empty ledger

verification.note: `useState(currentYear - 1)` opens the page on 2025 against a ledger holding only 2026 rows. Defensible in January when filing last year's return, wrong the rest of the year. Filed independently by all three runs; every one of them read the empty year as a failed import, which is the failure mode that makes it major rather than cosmetic. Merged: runs 4 and 5 filed the same root cause under `tax-page-defaults-to-wrong-year`, which is the canonical id -- it names the default rather than the symptom. Both personas noticed the collision themselves and neither re-filed.

why_it_matters: I read tax exposure at decision time, per my mandate. If I trust the first screen I land on, I would conclude the tax page has not picked up my trading yet and stop checking it -- exactly the wrong read one session before I need this page's wash-sale panel to size an exit. A new user with a real book would reasonably conclude the import failed.

expected: The date the caption promises should be printed in the row -- 'Safe to repurchase on 2026-08-08' or equivalent -- not just a status word I have to trust. My mandate is literal about provenance: a number (or in this case a date-gated verdict) I cannot reconstruct from the page is one I will not act on, and right now the only way to see the actual date is to open devtools and read the API response myself.
observed: After selling QQQ at a loss this session, the /tax page's new 'Wash sales by symbol' table shows a row: SYMBOL=QQQ, DEFERRED=$0.00, PERMANENTLY DISALLOWED=$0.00, LOSS SALES=1, LAST LOSS SALE=2026-07-08, REPURCHASE STATUS='SAFE TO REPURCHASE'. No date appears anywhere in the row or the panel. The caption directly under the table reads 'This date tells you when a new purchase will stop creating a new wash sale on this symbol's most recent loss sale' -- promising a date that is nowhere on the page. I fetched the underlying data directly (GET /api/tax/report?year=2026) and the API already computes and returns the exact figure the caption describes: wash_sale_summary.symbols[0].repurchase_safe_on = '2026-08-08', alongside days_until_safe and window_is_open. The frontend drops this field and renders only the boolean-shaded status word.
repro: Sell a position at a loss (session 3: sold 2 QQQ at 704.60, cost basis 714.53/sh).
Navigate to /tax, select the tax year containing the sale.
Read the 'Wash sales by symbol' table -- the QQQ row shows a Repurchase Status of 'SAFE TO REPURCHASE' with no date in the row or column.

Compare against GET /api/tax/report?year=2026 -- wash_sale_summary.symbols[0].repurchase_safe_on is populated ('2026-08-08' in this run), proving the backend already has the value the frontend does not show.
suggested_fix: Render wash_sale_summary.symbols[].repurchase_safe_on directly in the Repurchase Status cell (e.g. 'Safe to repurchase on 2026-08-08') instead of only a derived status word.
title: Wash-sale per-symbol panel's repurchase-safe date is computed but never rendered

verification.note: The claim as filed -- 'the frontend never renders it' -- is false: Tax.tsx:762 renders `{days_until_safe} days - safe from {repurchase_safe_on}` whenever the window is open. The date is dropped only in the window-closed branch (line 766), where a bare 'safe to repurchase' badge is shown while the caption below still promises a date. Real gap, narrower than reported. Both personas landed in the closed branch because `window_is_open` is computed from the real clock (washsale_summary.py:142) while the replay is July, so every July window had long closed.

why_it_matters: This is exactly the decision this panel exists for: whether I can safely rebuy a name I just sold at a loss without triggering a wash sale. 'Safe to repurchase' with no date is an assertion, not a number -- I have no way to tell whether that status is fresh, how many days of margin it has, or when it will flip if I check back tomorrow. For a symbol still inside the window, the same missing-date problem would leave me guessing at exactly the date I most need to know.
